at indfri.explanation: "At indfri" means "to fulfill / redeem". To say you keep a promise, use it with "et løfte" (a promise): "Hun indfrier sit løfte" (She fulfills her promise). To say you pay off a loan completely, use "et lån" (a loan): "Jeg vil indfri lånet" (I want to pay off the loan).

at indføre.explanation: "At indføre" means "to introduce (a rule)". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at føre" (to lead). To say a town starts new rules, use it with the rules: "Kommunen indfører nye regler" (The municipality is introducing new rules). To introduce one person to another, use "at præsentere" (to present): "Må jeg præsentere min ven?" (May I introduce my friend?).

at indgive.explanation: "At indgive" means "to submit / file". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at give" (to give). To say you hand an official application to an office, use it with "en ansøgning" (an application): "Hun indgav en ansøgning" (She submitted an application).

at indgå.explanation: "At indgå" means "to enter into (an agreement)". To say two people get married, use it with "ægteskab" (marriage): "De indgår ægteskab" (They are getting married). To say something is part of a whole, add "i" (in) after it: "Mel indgår i opskriften" (Flour is part of the recipe).

at indhente.explanation: "At indhente" means "to catch up with". To say you make up for lost time, use it with "det forsømte" (what was missed): "Jeg vil indhente det forsømte" (I want to make up for what was missed). To say you get quotes from companies, use it with "tilbud" (offers): "Vi indhenter tilbud" (We are getting quotes).

at indikere.explanation: "At indikere" means "to indicate". To say a measurement points toward a result, use it with "at" (that) after it: "Målingerne indikerer, at det bliver koldt" (The measurements indicate that it will be cold).

at indkalde.explanation: "At indkalde" means "to call in / summon". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at kalde" (to call). To say a court orders people to come, say: "Retten indkalder vidner" (The court summons witnesses). To say you call a meeting, add "til" (to) before it: "Jeg indkalder til møde" (I am calling a meeting).

at indkøbe.explanation: "At indkøbe" means "to purchase". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at købe" (to buy). To talk about everyday shopping, use "at købe ind" (to shop) instead: "Jeg skal købe ind i dag" (I have to go shopping today).

at indlede.explanation: "At indlede" means "to begin / introduce". To say someone opens a meeting, use it with "mødet" (the meeting): "Han indleder mødet" (He opens the meeting). To say you start a relationship, use it with "et forhold" (a relationship): "De indleder et forhold" (They are starting a relationship).

at indrette.explanation: "At indrette" means "to furnish / set up". To say you are furnishing a home, use it with the home: "De indretter lejligheden" (They are furnishing the flat). With "sig" (oneself) it means "to settle in": "Vi indretter os i den nye lejlighed" (We are settling in at the new flat).

at indrette sig.explanation: "At indrette sig" means "to adapt / settle in". To say you adapt to a situation, add "efter" (according to): "Vi må indrette os efter vejret" (We have to adapt to the weather). To say you settle in a new home, add "i" (in): "Hun indretter sig i huset" (She is settling in at the house). Without "sig" (oneself), "at indrette" means "to furnish": "Hun indretter værelset" (She is furnishing the room).

at indrømme.explanation: "At indrømme" means "to admit". To say you admit something, you can start with "Jeg må indrømme" (I have to admit): "Jeg må indrømme, at jeg tog fejl" (I have to admit that I was wrong).

at indsamle.explanation: "At indsamle" means "to collect". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at samle" (to gather). To talk about collecting as a hobby, use "at samle" instead: "Jeg samler på frimærker" (I collect stamps).

at indse.explanation: "At indse" means "to realize". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at se" (to see). To say you understood something too late, say: "Jeg indså for sent, at det var en fejl" (I realized too late that it was a mistake).

at indsende.explanation: "At indsende" means "to submit". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at sende" (to send). To say you send in an application, use it with "ansøgning" (application): "Jeg har indsendt min ansøgning" (I have submitted my application).

at indskrænke.explanation: "At indskrænke" means "to restrict". To say you cut down how much you spend, use it with "forbruget" (the spending): "Vi indskrænker forbruget" (We are cutting down spending). To say freedom is limited, use it with "friheden" (the freedom): "Loven indskrænker friheden" (The law restricts freedom).

at indstille.explanation: "At indstille" means "to adjust / set". To say you set a device, use it with the device: "Jeg indstiller uret" (I am setting the clock). To say you put someone forward for a job or prize, use it with "en kandidat" (a candidate): "De indstiller en kandidat" (They are nominating a candidate).

at indstille sig på.explanation: "At indstille sig på" means "to prepare for / adjust to". To say you get ready for something that is coming, say: "Vi må indstille os på en kold vinter" (We must prepare for a cold winter). To say you have accepted a change, say: "Jeg har indstillet mig på at flytte" (I have accepted that I will move).

at indsætte.explanation: "At indsætte" means "to insert / deposit". To say you put money into a bank account, say: "Jeg indsætter penge på kontoen" (I am depositing money in the account). To say you put something into a text, say: "Jeg indsætter et billede i teksten" (I am inserting a picture into the text). To take money out, use "at hæve" (to withdraw): "Jeg vil hæve tusind kroner" (I want to withdraw a thousand kroner).

at indtage.explanation: "At indtage" means "to consume / take". To say how medicine must be taken, say: "Medicinen skal indtages med vand" (The medicine must be taken with water). To say soldiers capture a place, say: "Soldaterne indtog byen" (The soldiers captured the town).

at informere.explanation: "At informere" means "to inform". To name the topic, add "om" (about) before it: "Jeg informerer dig om mødet" (I am informing you about the meeting).

at insistere.explanation: "At insistere" means "to insist". To say what you insist on, add "på" (on) before it: "Jeg insisterer på en undskyldning" (I insist on an apology).

at inspirere.explanation: "At inspirere" means "to inspire". To say a book gave you ideas, say: "Bogen inspirerede mig" (The book inspired me). To say you were inspired by something, use "at blive inspireret af" (to be inspired by): "Jeg blev inspireret af filmen" (I was inspired by the film).

at installere.explanation: "At installere" means "to install". To ask someone to install a program, say: "Kan du installere appen?" (Can you install the app?). To say you remove it again, add "af" (off) to the front: "Jeg afinstallerer spillet" (I am uninstalling the game).

at integrere.explanation: "At integrere" means "to integrate". To say newcomers are made part of a society, say: "at integrere flygtninge" (to integrate refugees). To say you become part of a group yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Han har integreret sig godt" (He has integrated well).

at intensivere.explanation: "At intensivere" means "to intensify". To say the police search harder, use it with the search: "Politiet intensiverer eftersøgningen" (The police are intensifying the search).

at interessere.explanation: "At interessere" means "to interest". To say a thing interests you, put the thing first: "Fodbold interesserer mig" (Soccer interests me). To say you are interested, use "interesseret" (interested) with "i" (in): "Jeg er interesseret i fodbold" (I am interested in soccer).

at interessere sig for.explanation: "At interessere sig for" means "to be interested in". To say you are interested in something, use "mig" (myself): "Jeg interesserer mig for musik" (I am interested in music). To say a woman is, use "sig" (herself): "Hun interesserer sig for kunst" (She is interested in art). Without "sig" and "for", "at interessere" means "to interest": "Musik interesserer mig" (Music interests me).

at interviewe.explanation: "At interviewe" means "to interview". English speakers should remember the final "e" in the spelling. To say a journalist questions a politician, say: "Journalisten interviewer ministeren" (The journalist interviews the minister).

at introducere.explanation: "At introducere" means "to introduce". To say you bring in something new, say: "Firmaet introducerer en ny telefon" (The company is introducing a new phone). To introduce one person to another, use "at præsentere" (to present) instead: "Må jeg præsentere Anna?" (May I introduce Anna?).

at invadere.explanation: "At invadere" means "to invade". To say an army enters a country, say: "Hæren invaderer landet" (The army is invading the country). To say a place is filled with many people, say: "Turisterne invaderer byen" (The tourists are invading the town).

at investere.explanation: "At investere" means "to invest". To say what you put money into, add "i" (in) after it: "Hun investerer i en lejlighed" (She is investing in a flat). To say you put time into something, say: "Jeg investerer mange timer i projektet" (I am investing many hours in the project).

at invitere.explanation: "At invitere" means "to invite". To invite someone for coffee, add "på" (for) after the person: "Må jeg invitere dig på kaffe?" (May I invite you for coffee?).

at irritere.explanation: "At irritere" means "to irritate". To say a noise annoys you, say: "Larmen irriterer mig" (The noise annoys me). To say you are annoyed, use "irriteret" (annoyed): "Jeg er irriteret" (I am annoyed).

at isolere.explanation: "At isolere" means "to isolate / insulate". To say you insulate a building against cold, say: "Vi isolerer loftet" (We are insulating the attic). To say a person is kept away from others, say: "Patienten bliver isoleret" (The patient is being isolated).

en iagttager.explanation: "En iagttager" means "an observer". It comes from the verb "at iagttage" (to observe): "Jeg iagttager fuglene fra vinduet" (I watch the birds from the window).

en identitet.explanation: "En identitet" means "an identity". To talk about the identity of a country, use "national" (national): "en national identitet" (a national identity).

en idrætshal.explanation: "En idrætshal" means "a sports hall". It is built from "idræt" (sports) and "en hal" (a hall). To say you have the school subject, use "idræt" alone: "Vi har idræt i morgen" (We have PE tomorrow).

en idé.explanation: "En idé" means "an idea". To say you get an idea, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik en idé" (I got an idea). To say you have no idea, say: "Jeg aner det ikke" (I have no clue).

en igangsætter.explanation: "En igangsætter" means "an initiator". It comes from "at sætte i gang" (to set something going): "Vi sætter projektet i gang" (We are getting the project started).

en illusion.explanation: "En illusion" means "an illusion". To say you have no false hopes about something, say: "Jeg har ingen illusioner om det" (I have no illusions about it).

en illustration.explanation: "En illustration" means "an illustration". It comes from the verb "at illustrere" (to illustrate): "Tegneren illustrerer bogen" (The artist illustrates the book). To say an example makes a point clear, say: "Det er en god illustration af problemet" (That is a good illustration of the problem).

en implikation.explanation: "En implikation" means "an implication". To ask what a decision leads to, use the plural: "Hvad er implikationerne?" (What are the implications?)

en indbakke.explanation: "En indbakke" means "an inbox". It is built from "ind" (in) and "en bakke" (a tray). "Bakke" also means "hill", as in "Cyklen ruller ned ad bakken" (The bike rolls down the hill).

en indblanding.explanation: "En indblanding" means "an interference". To say someone dislikes others getting involved, say: "Hun bryder sig ikke om andres indblanding" (She does not like other people butting in).

en indbygger.explanation: "En indbygger" means "an inhabitant". To say how many people live in a place, say: "Byen har 50.000 indbyggere" (The town has 50,000 inhabitants).

en inddragelse.explanation: "En inddragelse" means "an involvement". To say people take part in a decision, say: "inddragelse af borgerne" (involving the residents). Do not mix it up with "indblanding" (interference): "Hun bryder sig ikke om andres indblanding" (She does not like other people butting in). To say a license is taken away officially, say: "inddragelse af kørekort" (taking away a driver's license).

en inder.explanation: "En inder" means "an Indian". It comes from the country "Indien" (India). To say food is Indian, use "indisk" (Indian): "indisk mad" (Indian food). Do not mix it up with "en indianer" (a Native American): "Mange indianere boede i Nordamerika" (Many Native Americans lived in North America).

en inderside.explanation: "En inderside" means "an inside". It is built from "inder" (inner) and "en side" (a side). To say a page number, "side" also means "page": "side 12" (page 12).

en indflydelse.explanation: "En indflydelse" means "an influence". To say you have influence over something, use "at have indflydelse på" (to have influence on): "Jeg har ingen indflydelse på det" (I have no say in it).

en indflytning.explanation: "En indflytning" means "a move-in". It is built from "ind" (in) and "en flytning" (a move). To say you move into a new home, use the verb "at flytte ind" (to move in): "Vi flytter ind på fredag" (We are moving in on Friday).

en indflytningsgave.explanation: "En indflytningsgave" means "a housewarming gift". It is built from "indflytning" (moving in) and "en gave" (a gift). "Gave" also appears in "en julegave" (a Christmas present).

en indfødsretsprøve.explanation: "En indfødsretsprøve" means "a citizenship test". It is built from "indfødsret" (citizenship) and "en prøve" (a test). The test is about Danish society, history and culture.

en indgang.explanation: "En indgang" means "an entrance". It is built from "ind" (in) and "en gang" (a passage). "Gang" also means "hallway", as in "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway).

en indkaldelse.explanation: "En indkaldelse" means "a summons / notice". It comes from the verb "at indkalde" (to call in). To say you got a notice for a meeting, add "til" (to): "indkaldelse til generalforsamling" (notice of a general meeting).

en indkomst.explanation: "En indkomst" means "an income". To say income tax, put "skat" (tax) after it: "indkomstskat" (income tax). To talk about a whole year, use "årlig" (yearly): "årlig indkomst" (yearly income).

en indkøbskurv.explanation: "En indkøbskurv" means "a shopping basket". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "en kurv" (a basket). Do not mix it up with "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart on wheels): "Indkøbsvognene står ved indgangen" (The shopping carts are by the entrance).

en indkøbsliste.explanation: "En indkøbsliste" means "a shopping list". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "en liste" (a list). "Indkøb" also appears in "at gå på indkøb" (to go shopping): "Jeg går på indkøb" (I am going shopping).

en indkøbspose.explanation: "En indkøbspose" means "a shopping bag". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "en pose" (a bag). "Pose" also names a bag of food, as in "en pose chips" (a bag of chips).

en indkøbstur.explanation: "En indkøbstur" means "a shopping trip". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "en tur" (a trip). "Tur" also appears in "en cykeltur" (a bike ride).

en indkøbsvogn.explanation: "En indkøbsvogn" means "a shopping cart". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "en vogn" (a cart). "Vogn" also appears in "en barnevogn" (a baby stroller).

en indkørsel.explanation: "En indkørsel" means "a driveway". It is built from "ind" (in) and "kørsel" (driving). To read a road sign, "Indkørsel forbudt" means "No entry" for cars.

en indledning.explanation: "En indledning" means "an introduction". To say where something is written in a text, say: "Det står i indledningen" (It says so in the introduction). To introduce a person, use "at præsentere" (to introduce) instead: "Må jeg præsentere min kollega?" (May I introduce my colleague?).

en indlæggelse.explanation: "En indlæggelse" means "a hospitalization". It comes from the verb "at indlægge" (to admit): "Han er indlagt" (He has been admitted). For treatment without an overnight stay, use "ambulant" (outpatient): "en ambulant behandling" (an outpatient treatment).

en indlæring.explanation: "En indlæring" means "a learning process". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at lære" (to learn). To say someone has trouble learning, add "vanskeligheder" (difficulties): "indlæringsvanskeligheder" (learning difficulties).

en indretning.explanation: "En indretning" means "a layout / furnishing". It comes from the verb "at indrette" (to furnish). To say you have furnished a room, say: "Vi har indrettet stuen" (We have furnished the living room).

en indretningsarkitekt.explanation: "En indretningsarkitekt" means "an interior designer". It is built from "indretning" (layout, furnishing) and "en arkitekt" (an architect).

en indsamling.explanation: "En indsamling" means "a collection (fundraiser)". To say you collect money for others, use "at samle ind" (to collect): "Vi samler penge ind" (We are collecting money). Do not mix it up with "en samling" (a collection of things you own): "Han har en stor samling frimærker" (He has a big collection of stamps).

en indsat.explanation: "En indsat" means "an inmate". It is the past form of "at indsætte" (to put in), so it literally means "put in".

en indsats.explanation: "En indsats" means "an effort". To say you make an effort, use "at gøre" (to do): "Jeg gør en indsats" (I am making an effort). To thank someone, say: "Tak for din indsats" (Thanks for your effort). To name a planned action against a problem, say: "en indsats mod ensomhed" (an effort against loneliness).

en indskrivning.explanation: "En indskrivning" means "an enrollment". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at skrive" (to write). To say when enrollment opens, say: "Indskrivningen begynder i januar" (Enrollment begins in January).

en indsprøjtning.explanation: "En indsprøjtning" means "an injection". To say you get a shot, use the shorter "en sprøjte" (a syringe): "Jeg skal have en sprøjte" (I am getting a shot). To say money is put into a business, say: "en økonomisk indsprøjtning" (a financial injection).

en indstilling.explanation: "En indstilling" means "a setting". To say you changed a setting on a phone or in an app, say: "Jeg har ændret indstillingen" (I have changed the setting). To say someone has an attitude, say: "Han har en positiv indstilling" (He has a positive attitude).

en indtægt.explanation: "En indtægt" means "an income". To say where money comes from, say: "Turisme er byens vigtigste indtægt" (Tourism is the town's main income). The opposite is "en udgift" (an expense): "Husleje er min største udgift" (Rent is my biggest expense).

en industri.explanation: "En industri" means "an industry". To name one kind of industry, put a word in front: "fødevareindustri" (food industry) and "medicinalindustri" (drug industry).

en indvandrer.explanation: "En indvandrer" means "an immigrant". It comes from the verb "at indvandre" (to immigrate): "Han indvandrede i 2010" (He immigrated in 2010).

en indånding.explanation: "En indånding" means "an inhalation / breath". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at ånde" (to breathe). To say you take a deep breath, use "dyb" (deep): "en dyb indånding" (a deep breath).

en infektion.explanation: "En infektion" means "an infection". To say where the infection is, put the body part before it: "en halsinfektion" (a throat infection). To say you caught one, use "at få" (to get): "Han har fået en infektion" (He has got an infection).

en influencer.explanation: "En influencer" means "an influencer". To say you follow one online, use "at følge" (to follow): "Jeg følger en influencer på Instagram" (I follow an influencer on Instagram).

en ingeniør.explanation: "En ingeniør" means "an engineer". To name the kind of engineer, put a word in front: "maskiningeniør" (mechanical engineer).

en ingrediens.explanation: "En ingrediens" means "an ingredient". To ask what a recipe needs, use the plural: "Hvilke ingredienser skal jeg bruge?" (Which ingredients do I need?) To name the list on a package, say "en ingrediensliste" (an ingredient list).

en innovation.explanation: "En innovation" means "an innovation". Do not mix it up with "en opfindelse" (an invention), a thing someone makes for the first time: "Telefonen er en vigtig opfindelse" (The telephone is an important invention).

en inspektør.explanation: "En inspektør" means "an inspector". To name the kind of inspector, put a word in front: "en fødevareinspektør" (a food inspector).

en inspiration.explanation: "En inspiration" means "an inspiration". To say you get ideas from somewhere, use "at hente" (to fetch): "Vi henter inspiration fra Italien" (We get inspiration from Italy).

en installation.explanation: "En installation" means "an installation". To say how long it takes to put in a program, say: "Installationen tager to minutter" (The installation takes two minutes). In art it means a work built in a room: "Kunstneren har bygget en installation i museet" (The artist has built an installation in the museum).

en institution.explanation: "En institution" means "an institution". In Denmark it is also the word for a daycare for children, such as "en vuggestue" (a nursery) or "en børnehave" (a kindergarten). To say a child goes there, say: "Vores søn er i institution" (Our son is in daycare).

en instruks.explanation: "En instruks" means "an instruction". To say someone did what the rules told them, say: "Han handlede efter instruks" (He acted according to instructions).

en instruktion.explanation: "En instruktion" means "an instruction". To tell someone to read the steps, use the plural: "Læs instruktionerne først" (Read the instructions first). Do not mix it up with "en instruktør" (a director): "Instruktøren leder filmen" (The director leads the film).

en instruktør.explanation: "En instruktør" means "a director". To say who leads a film, say: "Instruktøren leder filmen" (The director leads the film). To name a sports teacher, put the sport in front: "en svømmeinstruktør" (a swimming instructor). Do not mix it up with "en direktør" (a company director): "Direktøren leder firmaet" (The company director runs the firm).

en integration.explanation: "En integration" means "integration". To talk about newcomers becoming part of society, say: "integration af flygtninge" (integration of refugees). To talk about computer systems, say: "integration mellem to systemer" (integration between two systems).

en interesse.explanation: "En interesse" means "an interest". To name the subject of your interest, add "for" (in): "Han har stor interesse for biler" (He has a big interest in cars). To say you are interested, use "at være interesseret i" (to be interested in): "Jeg er interesseret i historie" (I am interested in history).

en internetforbindelse.explanation: "En internetforbindelse" means "an internet connection". It is built from "internet" and "en forbindelse" (a connection). To say you have no signal, say: "Jeg har ingen forbindelse" (I have no connection).

en invasion.explanation: "En invasion" means "an invasion". It comes from the verb "at invadere" (to invade). To say a crowd of tourists fills a place, say: "en invasion af turister" (an invasion of tourists).

en investering.explanation: "En investering" means "an investment". To say what you invest in, add "i" (in): "en investering i uddannelse" (an investment in education). To say something is worth the money, say: "Den nye cykel er en god investering" (The new bike is a good investment).

en invitation.explanation: "En invitation" means "an invitation". It comes from the verb "at invitere" (to invite). To say you accept, use "at takke ja" (to say yes, thanks): "Jeg takker ja til invitationen" (I accept the invitation).

en irritation.explanation: "En irritation" means "an irritation". It comes from the verb "at irritere" (to irritate). To say your skin is irritated, say: "en irritation i huden" (an irritation in the skin).

en isbjørn.explanation: "En isbjørn" means "a polar bear". It is built from "is" (ice) and "en bjørn" (a bear). "Is" also means "ice cream", as in "Jeg vil have en is" (I want an ice cream).

en isbod.explanation: "En isbod" means "an ice cream stand". It is built from "is" (ice cream) and "en bod" (a small stall). "Is" also means "ice", as in "Der er is på søen" (There is ice on the lake).

en isenkræmmer.explanation: "En isenkræmmer" means "a hardware dealer". It comes from "isenkram" (hardware, small things for the home). To say where you buy nails and screws, say: "Vi køber søm og skruer hos isenkræmmeren" (We buy nails and screws at the hardware store).

en islænding.explanation: "En islænding" means "an Icelander". It comes from the country "Island" (Iceland). To name the language, use "islandsk" (Icelandic): "Hun taler islandsk" (She speaks Icelandic). Do not mix it up with "en irlænder" (an Irishman): "En irlænder kommer fra Irland" (An Irishman comes from Ireland).
